## Design

### 2026-10-09 – #### October 9: Making progress on the Driver Deck PCB!!

**1.5h**

#### October 9: Making progress on the Driver Deck PCB!!

I started designing the PCB for my FRC 5719 Driver Deck using KiCad! The goal is to make a custom keyboard controller with WASD keys, four programmable buttons, an OLED screen, and RGB LEDs around the edge.

So far, I’ve worked on connecting the XIAO RP2040, the switches and diodes, and the OLED display. I also started wiring the RGB LEDs, including the level shifter and capacitor needed to help them work reliably.

There’s still work to do on the PCB layout and checking the connections, but the schematic is starting to come together!
I split my work session into 3 half hour sessions.
Session 1: Getting some footprints, and putting them down.
Session 2: Wiring.
Session 3: ERC Checking.

### 2026-10-10 – #### October 10: ERC DEBUGGING! GAHHHH

**2h**

#### October 10: ERC DEBUGGING! GAHHHH

So today I decided to actually read what the ERC said and let me tell you it is not fun at all. 40 ERRORS when i started half an hour in and I am at 43 I DONT EVEN KNOW HOW. Anyways i fixed some stuff by adding power flags and used the highlight tool and all my traces were fine but still had errors. ### 2026-10-10 – #### October 10: Finished the PCB on KiCad!

**2h**

#### October 10: Finished the PCB on KiCad!

So this isnt really the first time I have made a keypad. I made one for hackpad a long time ago but its been a couple of months.
Designing this was a really good refresher for me. Anyways, I finished the traces hopefully it isn't too expensive to be honest.
I also found some spares from my hackpad. So yeah I also ignored the ERC and fixed some wiring stuff theres a lot of through connections as well, Also I gave up on the LED stuff as it was too expensive. Now I am going to make a CAD Render of the pcb, and also going to start writing the firmware, also I am going to export the gerbers,
